newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope accepts invitation to visit Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Pope accepts invitation to visit Georgia.

text.p: Pope John Paul received Georgian president Eduard Shevardnadze in a private audience on Friday and accepted his invitation to visit the former Soviet republic, the Vatican said.

"President Shevardnadze invited the Pope to visit Georgia and the Caucasus region. John Paul accepted the invitation and was hopeful about the possibility of making a visit," chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said.
Navarro-Valls said the 76-year-old Polish Pope, who was influential in the fall of communism in Eastern Europe in 1989, discussed the changes in the region since the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.
While he was foreign minister of the Soviet Union, Shevardnadze was instrumental in reforms that helped end the Cold War.
If the Pope eventually goes to Georgia it would be his second visit to countries of the former Soviet Union after a trip to the Baltic states of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia in 1993.
Shevardnadze met the Pope at the end of a three-day official visit to Italy during which he held talks with Italian political leaders, businessmen and the three U.N. food agencies based in Rome.
Shevardnadze became president of Georgia in 1992, a year after it gained independence from the Soviet Union.
